subject: chemistry
title: Ligands and complex ions
key_idea: A complex ion is a central metal ion surrounded by ligands, each bonded by a lone pair in a coordinate bond. The coordination number sets the shape: six gives octahedral, four gives tetrahedral or square planar, two gives linear. Complexes can show cis-trans and optical isomerism.

blocks.text: This section covers what a ligand is and how ligands are classified by the number of bonds they make.

items.meaning: A molecule or ion with a lone pair of electrons that it donates to a central metal atom or ion.
A covalent bond where both shared electrons come from one atom. Also called a dative covalent bond.
A central metal ion surrounded by ligands.
The number of coordinate bonds to the central metal ion.

items: The metal ion accepts the lone pair into a vacant d orbital.
In [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ the coordination number is 6, because there are six bonds to copper.
Coordination number counts bonds, not ligands. A bidentate ligand makes two bonds.
H₂O, NH₃ and OH⁻ are monodentate because each uses one lone pair on one atom to bond.
A bidentate ligand has two atoms, each with a lone pair, that can both bond to the same metal ion.
EDTA⁴⁻ wraps round the metal ion using six lone pairs, so a single EDTA⁴⁻ gives six-fold coordination.
A ligand donates a lone pair, forming a coordinate bond.
Coordination number is the number of coordinate bonds.
Monodentate ligands make one bond, bidentate two, multidentate more.

blocks.text: The coordination number and the size of the ligand decide the shape. Pairs of ligands repel and sit as far apart as possible.

diagram.alt: Pick a complex ion to see its coordination number, shape and bond angle.

options.label: [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺
results: Six small ligands fit round the ion.

options.label: [CuCl₄]²⁻
results: Large Cl⁻ ligands: only four fit.

options.label: [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺
results: Two ligands, as far apart as possible.

items: Small ligands such as H₂O and NH₃ usually give six-fold, octahedral complexes.
Larger ligands such as Cl⁻ crowd the metal ion, so four fit, in a tetrahedral shape.
Square planar complexes are formed by some ions, for example platinum(II).
[Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ is the linear complex in Tollens' reagent.

items.text: Fe³⁺ with Cl⁻ ligands, four-fold coordination.

blocks.text: Uncharged ligands such as H₂O and NH₃ add nothing, so the complex has the same charge as the metal ion, for example [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺.

items: Six small ligands: octahedral, 90°. Four large ligands: tetrahedral, 109.5°.
Square planar is 90° and linear is 180°.
Overall charge = metal charge + sum of ligand charges.

blocks.text: Complexes with the same formula can have the ligands arranged differently. These are stereoisomers.

rows: Like ligands next to each other (cis) or opposite (trans)
Two forms that are non-superimposable mirror images

items: Square planar Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂: the cis form has both Cl on the same side. The trans form has them opposite.
Octahedral [Co(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺: the two H₂O are either next to each other (cis) or opposite (trans).
Optical isomers arise when three bidentate ligands wrap round a metal ion in an octahedral complex, as in [Ni(en)₃]²⁺.
The two optical isomers rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions.

items.meaning: Stereoisomerism where like ligands are on the same side (cis) or on opposite sides (trans) of the central ion.
Non-superimposable mirror images of the same complex.

items: Cis-platin is the cis isomer of Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂, used as an anti-cancer drug.
It binds to DNA in cancer cells, which stops the cells dividing.
It is supplied as the cis isomer only. The trans isomer does not bind to DNA in the same way, so it is not effective as a drug.
Cis-trans isomers differ in which side like ligands sit.
Optical isomers are non-superimposable mirror images.
Cis-platin binds to DNA and stops cell division.

checks.a: A molecule or ion with a lone pair of electrons that forms a coordinate (dative covalent) bond to a central metal atom or ion.

checks.q: Give the formula, including charge, of the complex formed by Co²⁺ and four Cl⁻ ligands. State its shape and bond angle.
Explain why cis-platin is used as a single isomer in cancer treatment.
checks.a: Cis-platin binds to DNA, preventing cell division. The trans isomer does not bind in the same way, so it would not be effective.

items: Be able to draw 3-D diagrams of isomers, using solid wedges and dashed lines for bonds that point towards and away from you.
An unfamiliar ligand is treated like any other: find the lone pairs, then count the bonds it can make to one ion.
Examples to know: octahedral [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ and [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺, tetrahedral CuCl₄²⁻ and CoCl₄²⁻, square planar Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂.
Identify bidentate ligands such as NH₂CH₂CH₂NH₂ and multidentate ligands such as EDTA⁴⁻ from their structures, by finding atoms with lone pairs that can bond to the same ion.
H₂O, OH⁻ and NH₃ are monodentate, forming octahedral complexes with six-fold coordination.
Relatively large ligands such as Cl⁻ give tetrahedral complexes.
Cis-trans isomerism is a special case of E-Z isomerism.
Octahedral complexes show cis-trans isomerism with monodentate ligands and optical isomerism with bidentate ligands.
Square planar complexes can show cis-trans isomerism. Cisplatin is the cis isomer.
Describe complexes of copper(II) and cobalt(II) with water, ammonia, hydroxide and chloride ligands.
Examples of ligands: monodentate H₂O, NH₃, Cl⁻, CN⁻; bidentate en and C₂O₄²⁻; polydentate EDTA⁴⁻.
Cis-trans isomerism also appears in octahedral [Co(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ and [Ni(en)₂(H₂O)₂]²⁺.
[Ni(en)₃]²⁺ and the cis form of [Ni(en)₂(H₂O)₂]²⁺ show optical isomerism.
A complex is polar if the bond dipoles do not cancel overall.
Cis isomers have like ligands on one side, so the dipoles add up and the complex is polar.
Trans isomers have like ligands opposite each other, so the dipoles cancel and the complex is non-polar.
